target_customer: Web teams running MySQL on Amazon EC2
problem: Running, backing up and recovering production databases in the cloud took scarce admin time.
business_model: Managed database service at a 10 to 20 percent markup over EC2 prices

founders.name: Justin Santa Barbara
founders.background_notes: CEO per TechCrunch Feb 2009; joined Meteor in Oct 2014 to lead real-time data work.

founders.name: Mark Kinsey
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page, noted as designing a phone interface later.

technical_complexity.rationale: Automating replication, backup and failover for relational databases on rented cloud servers was hard for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Built on standard MySQL so customers were not locked in by design, which also made leaving easy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Amazon launched RDS for MySQL in October 2009 and commentators said it would crush FathomDB; the company continued until Meteor hired its founder in 2014.

market_need_then: Teams were moving to EC2 in 2008 and 2009 and had to run their own databases there.

branding.domain_note: Used fathomdb.com, the exact .com; acquisition history not found.

brand_strength.rationale: No press on the brand found.

outcome_analysis: FathomDB launched in February 2009 as managed MySQL on EC2 but Amazon shipped RDS eight months later. The team kept going for years on small funding and in October 2014 Meteor announced it had acquired the company and that its creator would lead real-time data work. Terms were not disclosed and a directory says the service shut down, which fits a soft landing.
notes: Company site returned HTTP 503. Rounds rest on a single database each: PitchBook gives $150K in March 2008 and a total of $150K, Seedtable gives a Jan 2009 seed with no amount. PitchBook names Apollo GraphQL as acquirer, which conflicts with TechCrunch, InfoQ and PE International (Meteor); Meteor used. YC lists Inactive, consistent with the acquisition. Competitor list empty: a Hacker News mention of RightScale dates to 2009, after the batch, and Amazon RDS came later still. Alicia Collins as co-founder rests on the YC page only.
